LESSON: DATA PRESENTATION AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Data Handling and Probability
Topic 5.1: Data Presentation and Interpretation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Data Presentation and Interpretation, part of Data Handling and Probability in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we represent data? 2. How do we determine the mean of data?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collect data from their own experiences, for example size of shoes, height or test scores. Use a suitable scale to represent the data in bar graphs. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers or teacher to perform the task.

2. discuss in purposive pairs or groups and interpret Bar graphs. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text- to-speech application/ point/sign/write) 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collect data from their own experiences, for example size of shoes, height or test scores. Use a suitable scale to represent the data in bar graphs. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers or teacher to perform the task.
2. discuss in purposive pairs or groups and interpret Bar graphs. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text- to-speech application/ point/sign/write) 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Data Presentation and Interpretation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses and represents data in line graphs.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner discusses and interprets Bar graphs.

• Self-efficacy: as the learner collects data from their own experiences, for example size of shoes, height or test scores.

Values

Social cohesion: as the learner collects data from their own experiences, for example size of shoes, height or test scores.
